Phylogenomics, spatiotemporal transcriptional dynamics and Cis-regulatory architecture underlying the Portulaca oleracea antioxidant network under extreme salinity.

This study integrates multi-tissue RNA-Seq, qRT-PCR, comparative phylogenomics across 154 plant genomes, and condition-specific gene regulatory network modeling to characterize 436 antioxidant genes in the extreme halophyte Portulaca oleracea under chronic hypersalinity. It reveals spatiotemporal transcriptional dynamics and cis-regulatory architecture underlying the plant's antioxidant defense network across organs and developmental stages. The work provides a framework for understanding how extreme salinity tolerance is coordinated at the regulatory level in a xerohalophyte.

Gut microbes 2026-12-31 Medium

Deep longitudinal phenotyping of a single individual enables host-microbiome metabolic modeling over 3.6 years.

Researchers tracked one person's gut microbiome at 51 time points over 3.6 years, building time-point-specific metabolic models from metagenomic data and predicting microbial metabolic activity via flux balance analysis. They then compared microbial abundances and predicted metabolic fluxes against clinical inflammation biomarkers (CRP, lactoferrin, calprotectin). The work demonstrates that deep longitudinal sampling of a single individual can link microbiome composition and metabolism to host inflammatory state.

An integrative systems biology framework decodes peripheral blood transcriptomic signatures, systemic interactome networks, and candidate targets in lung squamous cell carcinoma.

This study applies an integrative systems-biology framework to peripheral blood transcriptomic data from lung squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) patients, aiming to uncover systemic gene-expression signatures and construct interactome networks. The authors identify candidate hub genes that may serve as blood-based biomarkers or therapeutic targets for LSCC. The work highlights the value of combining transcriptomics with network analysis to decode systemic host responses in cancer.

Plant-environment interactions (Hoboken, N.J.) 2026-12-01 Low

Beyond the Primary-Secondary Dichotomy: Toward a Unified Metabolic Perspective.

This review argues that the traditional division between primary and secondary metabolism in plants is conceptually outdated. The authors show that metabolic pathways share precursors, cofactors, regulation, and transport, and that metabolites can serve growth, signaling, defense, or stress roles depending on context. They call for a unified metabolic perspective that better reflects how metabolites are actually produced and function.

The Maladaptive Stress State: A Systems Framework for Chronic Disease Persistence.

This perspective proposes the Maladaptive Stress State (MSS) as a systems-level framework to explain why biologically diverse chronic diseases converge on persistent states of chronic inflammation, impaired repair, and reduced adaptive flexibility. The framework distinguishes disease-initiating lesions from the self-sustaining maladaptive state that persists after the original insult subsides, offering a unifying conceptual model for chronic disease persistence.

Meta-finetuning foundation models for generalizable biological image segmentation in ultra-low-data regimes.

MetaTune adapts foundation models for biological image segmentation by splitting learnable parameters into meta-parameters that improve generalization and non-meta parameters for task-specific tuning, building on the BLO-SAM bi-level meta-finetuning approach. The method is designed for ultra-low-data regimes where labeled images are scarce, aiming to make foundation models more generalizable across segmentation tasks.

Causal assessment of Bayesian gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptomics.

The authors present scstruc, an R package for learning Bayesian gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptomic data and for evaluating how accurately the learned network structures capture causal gene relationships. The work addresses a gap in widely available software for both Bayesian network inference and structural causal assessment in this setting.

Image-guided alignment of consecutive multi-modal tissue slides.

COAST is a new computational method that physically aligns consecutive tissue sections using only their microscopy images, without needing shared molecular features or manual annotations. This enables researchers to combine spatial transcriptomics and other spatial omics data from adjacent slides into a single unified multi-modal dataset. The authors show it performs comparably to existing single-modality alignment tools across different technologies, tissues, and resolutions.

Multi-omics-constrained kinetic models quantify pathway rewiring and predict metabolic vulnerabilities in BRCA1-deficient ovarian cancer.

The authors built near-genome-scale kinetic models of metabolism (over 2,100 reactions) constrained by multi-omics data for isogenic BRCA1 wild-type and BRCA1-mutant ovarian cancer cells. Using these models, they quantified how BRCA1 loss rewires metabolic pathways and identified 28 enzyme-mediated metabolic vulnerabilities, most of which map to existing or approved drugs. Independent DepMap data supported the predictions, suggesting the approach can prioritize drug targets in BRCA1-deficient cancers.

A single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas reveals the endodermal gene regulatory network underlying Arabidopsis stem gravitropism.

This study generated a single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas of the Arabidopsis stem to map the gene regulatory network controlling gravitropism. The authors identify the endodermal cell populations and transcriptional programs downstream of the SGR5/IDD15 transcription factor that link gravity perception to asymmetric growth. The atlas provides a cell-type-resolved framework for understanding how plants convert a physical gravity signal into directional growth.

PIANO enables generative modeling of gene expression and scales multi-omics integration to 100 million cells.

PIANO is a deep learning framework that uses a generative model of gene expression to integrate single-cell multi-omics data. It addresses three key challenges: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells (demonstrated up to 100 million), and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. This enables more accurate comparisons across large-scale transcriptomic atlases.

Host-like temperature unlocks glucose uptake and metabolism in pathogenic Leptospira.

Using transcriptome-integrated genome-scale metabolic modeling, the authors show that host-like temperature (37°C) enables pathogenic Leptospira to take up and metabolize glucose, contrary to the long-held view that this pathogen relies mainly on long-chain fatty acids. This temperature-dependent metabolic shift may be important for survival and virulence within the mammalian host.

Network inference at single-cell resolution reveals morphoregulatory divergence and multilayered buffering in limb evolution.

This study compares mouse and pig limb development using single-cell transcriptomics and chromatin accessibility, combined with cross-species label transfer and gene regulatory network inference. It finds broadly conserved cellular organization but discrete divergence in HOX-, FGF-, and SHH-regulated programs, and shows that FGFR inhibition in mouse limb buds phenocopies the distal expansion of pig GREM1 expression. The work reveals morphoregulatory divergence and multilayered buffering in how conserved developmental programs produce morphological evolution.

Engineering rhizosphere microbial consortia for soil bioremediation: Mechanisms, field constraints, and evidence-based design.

Bioinformatics (Oxford, England) 2026-11-02 Medium

scPhyloGRN: gene regulatory network inference guided by lineage topology in single-cell developmental data.

scPhyloGRN introduces a method for inferring gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptomic data by explicitly incorporating the lineage topology (phylogenetic relationships) among individual cells. This helps disentangle expression variation due to shared ancestry from that due to cell state, improving regulatory inference in developmental contexts. The approach addresses a key challenge in single-cell GRN inference where both lineage and state confound expression patterns.

A time-resolved single-nucleus atlas of cochlear aging reveals biphasic inflammaging and Tbx2-dependent inner hair cell maintenance.

This study builds a time-resolved single-nucleus atlas of the aging cochlea, tracking how different cell types change over time. It identifies two distinct phases of age-related inflammation (biphasic inflammaging) and shows that the transcription factor Tbx2 is required for maintaining inner hair cells. The work integrates cell-cell communication, gene regulatory network reconstruction, and bulk validation across cohorts.

Protamine gene expression is associated with sperm motility in rams: An integrative experimental and gene network analysis.

This study examined whether expression levels of the protamine genes PRM1 and PRM2 correlate with semen quality in rams, using 15 ejaculates from five animals assessed by computer-assisted sperm analysis. Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.

The authors propose a meta-learning approach to gene regulatory network inference that arbitrates disagreements between ten existing inference methods on a per-edge basis, using a gradient-boosted classifier trained on the raw scores each method assigns. They also develop a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflicts. Evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens, the approach aims to outperform both single-method selection and simple averaging.

A pathogen-free citrus model recapitulates Huanglongbing-associated molecular and physiological reprogramming.

The authors created a pathogen-free citrus model by silencing two chloroplast biosynthesis genes (PDS and ALAD) using a virus vector, thereby disrupting carotenoid and chlorophyll production in Citrus macrophylla. This chloroplast dysfunction reproduced key molecular and physiological features of Huanglongbing (HLB), suggesting that host-driven chloroplast impairment—rather than the pathogen alone—contributes substantially to HLB symptom development. The system provides a tractable tool for dissecting host processes in HLB without needing the unculturable pathogen.

Causality analysis of toxicological mechanisms in networked systems such as adverse outcome pathway networks.

This paper argues that traditional causality frameworks like Koch's postulates and Bradford Hill criteria are insufficient for analyzing toxicological mechanisms in complex networked systems such as Adverse Outcome Pathway networks and multi-omics data. It synthesizes a modern causality toolbox—including directed acyclic graphs for making causal assumptions explicit and quantitative methods—to better handle multifactorial, nonlinear, and feedback-driven mechanisms in toxicology.

BoolFunc-EA: A Boolean-evolutionary approach for accurate inference of gene regulatory networks from time-series gene expression data.

BoolFunc-EA introduces a Boolean-evolutionary algorithm for inferring gene regulatory networks from time-series expression data, aiming to overcome scalability limits, local optima, and inaccurate mutual information estimates that affect existing Boolean network methods.
